nodes.description: Beta blockers are the first-line drug for symptomatic obstructive disease, reducing heart rate and contractility and lengthening diastolic filling. Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (verapamil, diltiazem) are the second-line alternative when beta blockade is ineffective or contraindicated, and disopyramide is added for refractory obstruction, though its side effects mean many centres use it as a bridge to septal reduction rather than as durable therapy. None of this is MYL2-specific; it is the disease-class therapy a symptomatic carrier receives.

nodes.description: In the MYL2 E22K founder cohort, hypertension was the single most common additional hypertrophy driver among carriers who went on to develop clinical disease. This is not the usual "environmental risk factor" relationship, in which an exposure raises risk at the margin: here the genotype on its own largely failed to produce disease, and the co-factor supplied the rest. The authors' practical conclusion follows from that — screen carriers for hypertension early and treat it, and do not exclude hypertensive individuals from genetic studies of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on the grounds that their hypertrophy is explained.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion in CMH10 is a variant in MYL2, encoding the ventricular regulatory myosin light chain (RLC) that binds the lever-arm region of beta-cardiac myosin. In the common dominant form the variant is a missense change (archetype R58Q) incorporated into the sarcomere; in the rare severe recessive form biallelic loss-of-function abolishes normal RLC. Either way the lesion perturbs how the myosin lever arm transmits force and how the myofilament responds to calcium.

nodes.description: The archetypal MYL2 allele and the one behind almost all of the functional work in this entry. Unlike E22K it is malignant: early onset, premature sudden death, and co-segregation across a four-generation pedigree. Its functional signature is unusually well resolved — reduced RLC Ser15 phosphorylation, stabilisation of the super-relaxed myosin state, lower maximal force with higher ATPase, increased calcium sensitivity with reduced cooperativity, and slower cross-bridge kinetics — and a Ser15 phosphomimetic reverses several of these in vitro. The two unaffected juvenile carriers in the four-generation pedigree are the age-related penetrance recorded in this entry's inheritance block seen within one family, not evidence against the allele.

nodes.description: Cardiomyocytes differentiated from induced pluripotent stem cells of a patient with MYL2-R58Q apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Its value is that it shows hypertrophy, disarray and calcium abnormality arising from the human genotype alone, in cells that have never experienced a pressure load — which separates the cell-autonomous consequences of the allele from the consequences of living in a hypertrophied heart.

Loss of the parallel alignment of cardiomyocytes, the pathognomonic lesion of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, is reproduced in human cardiomyocytes carrying the patient's own MYL2-R58Q allele — twice the rate seen in control cells.

nodes.description: The hypertrophy of MYL2 disease is not confined to the septum. The original description called the light chain form a rare variant of cardiac hypertrophy and located its lesion at the cardiac papillary muscles, without characterising an obstruction; mid-ventricular obstruction is attached specifically to the A13T allele in the later literature, and an apical distribution has been characterised for R58Q. Recording the distribution matters clinically, because a mid-cavity or apical pattern is what makes the diagnosis easy to miss on a study reported as normal septal thickness.

nodes.description: The regulatory light chain carries a conserved Ser15 phosphorylation site through which cardiac myosin light-chain kinase tunes force production. The R58Q allele lowers RLC phosphorylation in vivo, and this is allele-selective rather than a general property of HCM-associated RLC variants — the N47K allele, studied in the same transgenic series, did not reduce it. The deficit is mechanistically load-bearing rather than incidental: substituting an aspartate at the phosphorylation site to mimic the phosphorylated state restores force in R58Q-reconstituted fibres.

nodes.description: MYL2 encodes the regulatory light chain of heart ventricle and slow-twitch skeletal muscle simultaneously, and human pedigrees of light chain disease report cardiac hypertrophy together with abnormal skeletal muscle. Whether the skeletal deficit is a parallel local action of the allele or a systemic consequence of the cardiac disease is not settled, and the leading model argues against the simple parallel reading: in R58Q transgenic mice the soleus shows the same contractile deficit as ventricular papillary muscle and the fast-twitch extensor digitorum longus does not, but the transgene is cardiac-restricted, so the mutant light chain is not present in soleus at all. The authors present this as their surprising result rather than as evidence of local action. The human expression fact makes skeletal muscle a candidate direct target; the mouse experiment does not test it.

nodes.description:
Striated-muscle myosin partitions between an active force-producing state, a disordered-relaxed state whose heads can reach actin, and a super-relaxed (SRX) state with an ordered arrangement along the thick filament and a very low ATP turnover rate. R58Q shifts the equilibrium toward SRX in both reconstituted fibres and transgenic papillary muscle, leaving fewer heads recruitable. This direction matters clinically: the licensed cardiac myosin inhibitors for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy act by *increasing* SRX occupancy, so an allele that already stabilises SRX is not obviously the one that class was designed for. That reservation is a mechanistic inference, not a reported treatment failure, and is recorded as an open question rather than as guidance.
The ATP-turnover annotation on this node refers to the low turnover rate that defines the super-relaxed state itself. It is not in conflict with the raised actin-activated fibre ATPase reported for R58Q elsewhere in this entry: those are different measurements — the turnover of heads parked in the OFF state, and the enzymatic rate of the heads that are cycling.
nodes.id: Stabilization of the Myosin Super-Relaxed State

evidence.reference_title: Phosphomimetic-mediated in vitro rescue of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy linked to R58Q mutation in myosin regulatory light chain.
evidence.snippet: R58Q promotes the OFF state of myosin, both in reconstituted porcine fibers and in Tg mouse papillary muscles, thereby stabilizing the super-relaxed state (SRX) of myosin, characterized by a very low ATP turnover rate

nodes.description: Premature sudden death is the outcome that separates the malignant from the benign MYL2 alleles. It was the distinguishing feature of R58Q in the family screening study that also identified the benign E22K allele, and a four-generation pedigree carrying R58Q recorded three deceased members who died suddenly. No denominator exists — there is no MYL2-stratified outcome cohort — so this is a documented association and not a quantified risk.

nodes.description: The workhorse model of malignant MYL2 disease. It is the system in which the RLC phosphorylation deficit, the super-relaxed state shift, the diastolic abnormality, and the slow-twitch skeletal muscle deficit were each demonstrated. Its most useful property is that it is routinely studied alongside a Tg-N47K line carrying a milder RLC allele, so findings can be attributed to the malignant variant rather than to RLC transgenesis.

nodes.description: Sustained sarcomeric dysfunction produces the structural remodeling that defines HCM — cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, myofiber disarray, and interstitial fibrosis. RLC-mutant HCM classically involves mid-ventricular and papillary muscle hypertrophy, but the disarray-and-fibrosis substrate is shared with the other sarcomeric forms.
